video_summary.overall_goal: Open the Amaze file manager navigation drawer, navigate to the FTP Server screen, start the FTP server, take a screenshot of the running server, then navigate away (recents/home) and back to confirm the server is still running.
video_summary.description: The video shows Amaze file manager's root folder listing, the user opening the hamburger navigation drawer, selecting 'FTP Server' from the drawer, tapping START on the FTP Server screen (status changes from 'Not Running' to 'Secure Connection' with a generated ftps:// URL), taking a system screenshot, then backing out to the home screen (via quick-settings/notification panel showing the persistent 'Amaze FTP Server running' notification), and finally reopening the app to the FTP Server screen which still shows 'Secure Connection' / STOP.

steps.what_screen_is_visible: Amaze file manager showing /storage/emulated/0 with '23 folders and 1 files', a scrollable list of folders (._FilesByGoogle, Alarms, Android, AnkiDroid, Audiobooks, Autodesk, BlackPlayer, bseindia, DCIM, Documents, Download, Gcam...) and a pink '+' FAB.
steps.system_response: Navigation drawer begins sliding in from the left, partially covering the folder list.
steps.visual_feedback: Drawer overlay animates in over the folder list.
steps.intent_task: Open the navigation drawer to access app sections

steps.what_screen_is_visible: Full navigation drawer showing Internal Storage, SD card, quick folder shortcuts (DCIM, Download, Movies, Music, Pictures), Quick access, Recent files, Images, Videos, Audio, Documents, APKs, FTP Server, App Manager, Settings.
steps.system_response: Drawer closes and navigates to the FTP Server screen.
steps.visual_feedback: Drawer slides out; FTP Server screen fades in.
steps.intent_task: Navigate to the FTP Server feature

steps.what_screen_is_visible: FTP Server screen showing Status: Not Running, empty URL, empty Username/Password, Port: 2211, Shared Path: /storage/emulated/0, and a START button.
steps.visual_feedback: None yet visible in this step.

steps.what_screen_is_visible: Status now reads 'Secure Connection' (in green), URL populated as ftps://192.168.1.250:2211, Port: 2211, Shared Path unchanged, button now reads STOP.
steps.target_element: START button (already tapped, resulting state shown)
steps.system_response: Server is now running; a persistent system notification 'Amaze FTP Server running - now, at ftps://192.168.1.250:2211/' with a STOP action appears in the status bar / notification shade.
steps.visual_feedback: Status text turns green ('Secure Connection'); ongoing notification banner visible at top of screen.
steps.intent_task: Confirm the FTP server started successfully

steps.screen_name: FTP Server - Secure Connection (running), home screen visible behind notification
steps.what_screen_is_visible: Brief transition showing the notification banner 'Amaze FTP Server running... at ftps://192.168.1.250:2211/' with STOP action overlapping the FTP Server screen, then the device home screen (wallpaper with app icons: Amaze, AnkiDroid, K-9 Mail, NewPipe, WordPress) appears with the same notification still present.
steps.system_response: App backgrounds to the home screen; FTP server keeps running (notification persists).
steps.visual_feedback: Home screen wallpaper (blue/yellow crackled pattern) with dock icons and the persistent FTP notification banner still shown at top.
steps.intent_task: Leave the app while keeping the FTP server alive in the background

steps.what_screen_is_visible: Quick settings panel pulled down showing Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Hotspot, Airplane mode tiles, and below it the 'Amaze FTP Server running · now' notification with STOP action and a History chip; then panel dismissed showing 'No notifications' on plain quick-settings background.
steps.system_response: Notification shade opens, confirming the FTP server notification is still active; shade is then dismissed.
steps.visual_feedback: Notification panel slides down then closes back to home screen.
steps.intent_task: Verify the FTP server notification / background state

steps.what_screen_is_visible: Home screen showing app icons (Amaze, AnkiDroid, K-9 Mail, NewPipe, WordPress) at top and a second dock row (Chrome, Camera, etc.) at bottom; user taps the Amaze icon.
steps.system_response: Amaze relaunches, returning directly to the FTP Server screen (the last-viewed screen).
steps.visual_feedback: App icon tap triggers launch animation back into the app.
steps.intent_task: Reopen the app to verify server state persisted

steps.screen_name: FTP Server - Secure Connection (confirmed still running)
steps.what_screen_is_visible: FTP Server screen again showing Status: Secure Connection (green), URL: ftps://192.168.1.250:2211, Port: 2211, Shared Path: /storage/emulated/0, and a STOP button — matching the state from step 4, now confirmed to have persisted through backgrounding.
steps.system_response: No further changes; server remains running and screen remains static for the rest of the video.
steps.visual_feedback: Screen static, confirming the FTP server survived backgrounding without needing to be restarted.
steps.intent_task: Confirm the FTP server continues running after the app was backgrounded and reopened

overall_flow: Tap START on FTP Server screen -> status becomes 'Secure Connection' with generated ftps:// URL
Leave app (home/notification shade) while server keeps running in background (persistent notification)
Reopen Amaze app -> lands back on FTP Server screen
Confirm status still reads 'Secure Connection' / STOP, proving the server survived backgrounding
human_readable_step_summary: User opens the Amaze file manager's root storage folder view.
User taps the hamburger menu to open the navigation drawer.
User selects 'FTP Server' from the drawer.
On the FTP Server screen (initially 'Not Running'), user taps START.
The server starts: status turns green ('Secure Connection'), an ftps:// URL is shown, and a persistent system notification confirms the server is running.
User leaves the app (goes to home screen / checks notification shade) confirming the FTP notification persists in the background.
User reopens the Amaze app from the home screen.
The app returns to the FTP Server screen still showing 'Secure Connection' and STOP, confirming the server kept running across the app being backgrounded.
